function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data as specified by the parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

Sure thing! Here’s a quick rundown of where you can order a cake—whether you’re looking for something local, a specialty shop, or a nationwide service.

---

## 1️⃣ Local & Specialty Bakeries  
| What to Look For | Why It Matters | How to Order |
|------------------|----------------|--------------|
| **Independent bakeries** | Fresh, often handmade, unique flavors | Call or visit their website; many accept orders via email or a simple online form |
| **Farm‑to‑table or organic shops** | Ingredients sourced locally, often gluten‑free or vegan options | Check their menu online; some have a “Custom Orders” tab |
| **Artisan pastry chefs** | Signature creations, custom designs | Book a consultation or drop by the shop; many offer design services |

*Tip:* Ask about “pre‑order” policies—most bakeries need at least 24–48 hrs notice for custom cakes.

---

## 2️⃣ National Chains & Big Brands  
| Brand | Strength | Ordering Options |
|-------|----------|------------------|
| **Baker’s Dozen / Mrs. Fields** | Consistent quality, wide flavor range | Online store or phone order |
| **Dunkin’ Donuts** | Quick delivery, seasonal specials | Order through the Dunkin’ app or website |
| **Panera Bread** | Fresh, healthier options | Use the Panera app or call your local store |
| **Cinnabon** | Classic cinnamon rolls & cakes | Order online for pickup or delivery |

*Tip:* Many chains offer “gift card” options if you’re unsure about the exact cake size or flavor.

---

## 3️⃣ Online Delivery Platforms  
| Platform | Highlights | How to Use |
|----------|------------|------------|
| **Goldbelly** | Curated selection from top U.S. bakeries | Search by city or flavor, place order online |
| **BakeShare** | Community‑based, often local artisans | Browse listings, contact baker directly |
| **Etsy** | Handmade, custom designs | Filter by “cakes” and “delivery” |
| **Instacart** | Same‑day delivery from grocery stores | Add a cake to your cart, schedule delivery |
| **DoorDash / Uber Eats** | Many local bakeries partner for quick delivery | Search “cake” in your area, choose a vendor |

*Tip:* Check delivery fees and time windows—some platforms charge extra for same‑day or weekend deliveries.

---

## 4️⃣ Specialty & Custom Cake Designers  
| Designer | Specialty | Contact |
|----------|-----------|---------|
| **Cake Boss (Gordon Ramsay)** | Celebrity‑approved, Instagram‑ready | Website: cakeboss.com |
| **The Cake Studio** | Custom wedding & event cakes | Instagram @thecakestudio |
| **Sweet Treats Bakery** | Vegan & gluten‑free | Facebook page: SweetTreatsBakery |
| **Local Wedding Planners** | Often have preferred vendors | Ask your planner for recommendations |

*Tip:* For big events, book early (3–6 months) and bring a mood board or sample images.

---

## 5️⃣ DIY & “Build‑Your‑Own” Kits  
| Kit | Where to Buy | What You Get |
|-----|--------------|--------------|
| **Kraft Baking Kit** | Amazon, Walmart | Mix‑and‑bake cake mix + frosting |
| **Tasty Baking Co.** | Their website | Pre‑measured ingredients + recipe cards |
| **Home Chef** | Subscription box | Fresh ingredients + step‑by‑step guide |

*Tip:* Great for last‑minute orders or when you want to impress with a homemade touch.

---

## Quick Checklist Before You Order  
1. **Size & Shape** – 8‑inch round, 10‑inch square, tiered wedding cake, etc.  
2. **Flavor & Dietary Needs** – Vanilla, chocolate, gluten‑free, vegan, nut‑free.  
3. **Design & Theme** – Plain, frosted, fondant, edible images, custom toppers.  
4. **Delivery Time** – Same‑day, next‑day, or scheduled pickup.  
5. **Budget** – Prices vary widely; set a range before browsing.  

---

### Need a Recommendation for Your City?  
If you tell me your zip code or city, I can narrow down the best local bakeries or delivery options for you. Happy cake hunting! 🍰
